html:
SMTO-EXE-0091 — SMTO can't capture the screen in this Linux desktop mode

GUID: 54d9d443-c3ee-5009-8512-cd41ea1b20da
Slug: screen-compositor-denied
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: screen

What happened

  • The Linux computer running the Gateway uses Wayland, a desktop mode that SMTO's screenshots don't support yet. SMTO doesn't try to get around Wayland's screen protection, so nothing was captured.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On that Linux computer, sign out. On the login screen, pick an X11 or Xorg session (for example "GNOME on Xorg"), then sign in. SMTO's Linux screenshots only work in an X11 desktop session.
  2. Start the Gateway from inside that new desktop session. The Gateway checks which desktop mode it was started in, so one started under Wayland still can't capture.
  3. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Check connection for that Gateway, then start a New chat and ask again. Checking refreshes what the Gateway can do, and a new chat uses that updated list.

What success looks like

  • SMTO takes a screenshot on that computer instead of showing this error.

If it still fails

  • If that computer must stay on Wayland, screenshots from it aren't available in this version, but SMTO can still read text from image files there. Send the copied error details (Copy error details) to the person who manages that computer, and don't use tools that bypass Wayland's screen protection.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • LinuxScreen detected a Wayland session (WAYLAND_DISPLAY or XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland), for which this release has no consent-based capture backend.

What this means

  • Linux display enumeration detected Wayland through its session environment, for which this implementation has no consent-based capture backend. Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.

Why this can happen

  • Linux display enumeration detected Wayland through its session environment, for which this implementation has no consent-based capture backend.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the actual session type and advertised screen capabilities; do not route through XWayland to bypass compositor consent.

How to fix it

  • This release has no xdg-desktop-portal capture backend and deliberately never falls back to XWayland. Run the Gateway in an X11 session (DISPLAY set, XDG_SESSION_TYPE=x11), restart it and refresh its capabilities, or treat screen capture as unsupported on that host.
  • This release has no consent-based Wayland portal capture backend. Use an explicitly selected supported desktop session; do not bypass compositor security with XWayland.

Retry and execution caution

  • This release has no consent-based Wayland portal capture backend. Use an explicitly selected supported desktop session; do not bypass compositor security with XWayland.

How to verify the fix

  • An explicitly selected supported session handles the requested observation, or the unsupported requirement is reported.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass OS permissions, capture another Gateway, or copy screen content to diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
